::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[How to show that $ \sum_{n=0}^{2j} \frac {z^{n}}{\zeta^{n+1}} =\frac {z^{2j+1}-\zeta^{2j+1}}{(z-\zeta)\zeta^{2j+1}} $](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/4658954/how-to-show-that-sum-n-02j-frac-zn-zetan1-frac-z2j1), asked by [Aisha](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/846479/aisha) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2023-03-14; [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)):

> I am studying  some types of convergent sequences.
> I know that $\sum_{n=0}^{2j} z^{n}=\frac {z^{2j+1}-1}{z-1}$, but I am struggling with how to show that :
>
> $$\sum_{n=0}^{2j} \frac {z^{n}}{\zeta^{n+1}}=\frac {z^{2j+1}-\zeta^{2j+1}}{(z-\zeta)\zeta^{2j+1}}.$$
>
> When I examined this formula with $j=1$ and $j=2,$ it is works but how can I prove this formula for all values of $j=1,2,\dots$ or where can I find a list of table show this?
:::

As @Anne Bauval points out, this question has been answered in the comments. 

You are already aware of the geometric series formula. @dan_fulea suggests you change the variable from $z$ in your expression to $X$:
$$\sum_{n=0}^{2j} X^n = \frac{X^{2j+1}-1}{X-1}$$
Your expression contains a geometric series with $X=\frac{z}{\zeta}$ in it. So
$$\begin{aligned}
\sum_{n=0}^{2j} \frac {z^{n}}{\zeta^{n+1}}
    &= \frac{1}{\zeta}\sum_{n=0}^{2j} \left(\frac{z}{\zeta}\right)^n \\
    &= \frac{1}{\zeta} \cdot \frac{\left(\frac{z}{\zeta}\right)^{2j+1}-1}{\frac{z}{\zeta}-1} \\
    &= \frac{\left(\frac{z}{\zeta}\right)^{2j+1}-1}{z-\zeta} 
       \cdot \frac{\zeta^{2j+1}}{\zeta^{2j+1}}\\
    &= \frac {z^{2j+1}-\zeta^{2j+1}}{(z-\zeta)\zeta^{2j+1}}
\end{aligned}$$
